one_line: Restaurant back office where agent writes become costed, human-approved proposals.
what_it_does: Combines restaurant operational data with read-only agent investigation and blocked, cost-aware write proposals that a manager approves or rejects.
leverage_rationale: The blocked promise and shared live approval rail make WebMCP central: the agent can investigate freely, while consequential writes remain unresolved until a human decision returns to the tool call.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes 10 read-only tools and six write tools that build proposals and block until a human decides.
Transcript says approval includes supplier minimums, stockout timing, projected revenue and cash impact computed by the site.
Frames show a Tandem dashboard with structured records and an agent waiting/approval interface.
execution_rationale: Packaging and transcript present a highly coherent restaurant workflow with attributed decisions, costed proposals, rejection reasons and standing approvals; frame sheets show substantial dashboard/detail UI, though the contact sheets do not clearly prove a successful end-to-end completion.
execution_evidence: Video is 108 seconds with a detailed narrated workflow.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows orders table, Agent panel, refund proposal, cash movement and Approve/Reject controls.
Frame sheets show branded dashboard, tables, inspector panel, logs and warning states.
impact_rationale: Restaurant managers have a concrete high-stakes need for agent assistance without uncontrolled spending or operational changes; the product addresses that trust and context gap directly.
impact_evidence: Claimed deployment context is a three-branch restaurant chain with live orders and real money.
Narrative demonstrates supplier minimums, inventory runway and revenue consequences in the approval decision.
Human attribution and reversible/limited approvals are aligned to operational risk.
creativity_rationale: It reframes agent confirmation from a generic yes/no dialog into a site-owned, costed proposal and treats the unresolved tool call as a collaboration primitive.
creativity_evidence: Pitch's 'reads everything and changes nothing alone' model.
Proposal returns manager's reason to the agent and can prevent retry loops.
Standing approvals are scoped by change type, cash ceiling and uses.
usability_note: Clear manager rail, explicit risk/cost context, and approve/reject/reason flows suggest strong usability.
standouts: Costed, blocking approvals are a genuinely strong WebMCP-native control pattern.
Human decision context is returned to the agent rather than treated as a retry.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and a well-evidenced, high-stakes workflow.

one_line: WebMCP-native editor for agents to create animated architecture and workflow diagrams.
what_it_does: Lets agents and people co-edit structured diagrams, set motion/story steps, and export visual technical explanations from a shared canvas.
leverage_rationale: Structured diagram and animation tools are materially more reliable than UI driving for an agent, with undoable batches and shared canvas state.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies eight navigator.modelContext tools including replace_diagram, set_motion and set_story.
Claims typed visual grammar registry, auto-layout and incremental reversible edits.
Packaging screenshot visibly shows a diagram canvas and Presentation Steps panel.
execution_rationale: The packaging screenshot shows a coherent editor with a real architecture diagram, animate control, export/share controls and presentation steps; frame sheets show editor interaction, but no video and limited readable completion evidence cap confidence.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows Shopify order sequence diagram with connected nodes.
Visible 'Local save ready' status and green Animate control.
Frame sheets show canvas, nodes, side panels and editing states.
impact_rationale: Developers and technical teams have a real need to understand code/system impact; animated diagrams can improve review and communication, though the demonstrated audience fit is narrower than general coding tools.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets architecture, sequence and BPMN explanation of AI-made code changes.
About text identifies technical diagram creation as tedious and agent accessibility as a gap.
Visible Shopify order sequence is a concrete explanatory artifact.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-generated living diagrams, visual grammar and motion/story sequencing is a fresh synthesis beyond static diagram editors.
creativity_evidence: Animated architecture/workflow diagrams generated and refined by agents.
Shared human-agent canvas with every edit as one undoable batch.
Grammar registry spans UML, ER, BPMN and cloud icon systems.
usability_note: Visible editor structure, animation control and presentation-step rail indicate a usable authoring model, though frame text is small.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence is contact-sheet-only and does not visibly show an agent invocation.
standouts: Strong visual grammar and animation/story layer for technical diagrams.
advance_reason: High-leverage, original dev-tool concept with credible visible editor evidence.

one_line: AI-assisted workspace for building and repairing electrical single-line diagrams.
what_it_does: Creates structured electrical diagrams, validates engineering issues, and stages agent-proposed fixes for human review.
leverage_rationale: Electrical diagrams encode structured engineering constraints that an agent can inspect and repair more precisely through typed operations than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About describes build, review, fix-options, change-set and human review workflow.
Claims validation for missing parameters, cable sizing and protection warnings.
Frames show connected node canvas, selected element and right-side metrics/inspector.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a plausible engineering workflow and frames show a canvas and inspector, but low-resolution contact sheets obscure labels and do not establish end-to-end creation, validation and applied fix.
execution_evidence: Frames show project dashboard transitioning to connected diagram canvas.
Visible selected node and right-side results/configuration panel.
About claims staged change sets and engineering validation.
impact_rationale: Electrical engineers and designers face real complexity and repetitive parameter corrections; preserving constraints while proposing fixes could deliver meaningful niche value.
impact_evidence: About identifies buildings, factories, data centers, renewables, EV charging and industrial systems as users.
Specific issues include cable sizing and protection warnings.
Workflow preserves human review for engineering changes.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared agent-human state and staged change sets to professional electrical single-line engineering is an ambitious, differentiated domain application.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates on structured single-line diagram data rather than only pixels.
Build-review-fix-options-change-set workflow.
Domain-specific validation is central to the concept.
usability_note: The visible graph and inspector are plausible but small/obscured, and the workflow's exact controls are difficult to assess.
red_flags: No video and no public repository; image evidence is low-resolution and partly obscured.
standouts: Concrete professional engineering domain with structured repair constraints.
advance_reason: Strong impact and leverage potential warrant advancement despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Second-hand bookstore where every book is a unique copy.
what_it_does: Lets users or agents search one-off used books by metadata and interior notes, inspect details/excerpts, and reserve or release copies for 24 hours.
leverage_rationale: Structured search over condition and handwritten-note content plus reservation state is useful for an agent, though a general agent could achieve similar outcomes with some UI friction.
leverage_evidence: About specifies search by title, author, condition and note text.
Agent can inspect details/extracts and reserve or release a unique copy.
Shared live activity panel uses the same logic for human and agent.
execution_rationale: The packaging screenshot shows a coherent branded bookstore presentation, but there are no submitted video frames and the product UI/end-to-end reservation is not visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows Spanish project identity and book-themed media packaging.
About claims a ten-book catalog and 24-hour reserve/release workflow.
No frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Used-book shoppers and small sellers have a real discovery/reservation use case, especially where unique-copy availability matters, but the packet provides limited proof of breadth or depth.
impact_evidence: Explicit unique-copy second-hand bookstore model.
Search supports meaningful condition and inscription-like metadata.
Reservation prevents race-to-purchase for one-off inventory.
creativity_rationale: Treating the interior note and individuality of each used book as searchable product data gives a familiar storefront a memorable angle.
creativity_evidence: One-copy inventory is central rather than stock-infinite commerce.
Discovery by forgotten notes inside books is distinctive.
Spanish-language cultural framing is coherent.
usability_note: The described flow is simple and understandable, but actual storefront usability is not evidenced by frames.
red_flags: No video frame sheets; packaging screenshot is not product-run proof.
standouts: Unique-copy and interior-note search make the commerce scenario more than a generic cart.
advance_reason: Interesting concept but execution and WebMCP evidence are too thin relative to the stronger packets.

one_line: Agent-accessible short-link, QR-code and UTM attribution workspace.
what_it_does: Searches, creates and edits tracked short links, generates QR codes, and exposes analytics through WebMCP tools tied to an existing application.
leverage_rationale: The tools improve convenience and structured access but largely expose existing UI/backend capabilities; a general agent could accomplish comparable link and QR tasks with ordinary automation.
leverage_evidence: About explicitly says it is already existing software and 'handing out what a user can do normally'.
Tools mirror org-scoped REST endpoints used by the page.
Claims twelve tools, including link CRUD and analytics.
execution_rationale: The packet is technically coherent: auth-scoped endpoints, real UI reflection, output caps and Playwright testing; screenshots show the short-link/QR product, though no video or direct tool invocation is submitted.
execution_evidence: Frames show short-link/QR interface, forms and saved-link/attribution areas.
About details auth, org scoping, validation and real UI updates.
Demo is reported alive and public behavior is described.
impact_rationale: Marketing teams and operators have a concrete need to create trackable links and understand channel performance; the solution is useful even if not novel.
impact_evidence: Product supports UTM links, QR codes and channel click attribution.
Analytics include totals, top links and acquisition breakdowns.
Signed-in organization workflow is explicit.
creativity_rationale: This is a competent agent interface to an established short-link product, with limited novelty beyond the integration surface.
creativity_evidence: Existing software is explicitly retained with zero new backend.
WebMCP mirrors normal product actions and analytics.
usability_note: The familiar short-link workflow and direct UI reflection should be easy to use, subject to login.
red_flags: Pre-existing product with WebMCP primarily as an access layer.
No video evidence of agent invocation.
standouts: Thoughtful authorization, output-boundary and compatibility details.
advance_reason: Solid implementation but low WebMCP delta and creativity make it less competitive.

one_line: Trip-planning WebMCP tools that pair live weather/flights with disclosed sponsored recommendations.
what_it_does: Provides weather and deterministic flight search through native tools, attaching fail-open sponsored travel inventory to results.
leverage_rationale: Native callable trip tools and structured results are useful, but the same planning outcome is generally reachable through ordinary web search/automation; the distinctive delta is the ad delivery model rather than capability.
leverage_evidence: About specifies two real registerTool tools: get_weather and search_flights.
Weather uses Open-Meteo and flight search is deterministic.
Sponsored recommendation is disclosed and fail-open within tool results.
execution_rationale: The description is specific about tool behavior and production inventory, but there is no video and the submitted frame sheets are too small to prove a complete planner interaction.
execution_evidence: About gives concrete tool names and data sources.
Devpost packaging contains repeated promotional media for real tools and sponsored recommendations.
No video transcript or direct invocation evidence.
impact_rationale: Travelers can benefit from weather and flight context, while clearly disclosed recommendations may be relevant; value is plausible but the packet centers monetization infrastructure more than a deeply demonstrated planner.
impact_evidence: Trip planning is an identifiable audience and use case.
Weather and flight outputs are directly useful.
Sponsored content is explicitly disclosed.
creativity_rationale: Embedding disclosed live ad inventory inside real WebMCP results is a novel exploration of agent-era commercial infrastructure, even if trip planning itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Project directly tests whether a sponsored recommendation can live in a real tool result without becoming a banner.
Fail-open ad behavior and disclosure are part of the interaction model.
usability_note: The described two-tool flow is simple, but recommendation presentation and planner polish are not observable enough.
red_flags: No video; limited visual proof of live tool calls and planner completion.
standouts: Interesting, explicit experiment in disclosed sponsored agent-tool results.
advance_reason: Novel commercial angle, but thin product evidence and only moderate user-facing leverage.

one_line: Privacy-focused virtual makeup studio with an AI makeup artist.
what_it_does: Lets people try makeup on a live face preview, adjust exact shades and looks, and use an agent to read/apply coordinated studio state and find products.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supports shared state between natural-language intent and precise direct controls while keeping camera processing local; an agent driving controls would be less reliable and would require repeated restatement.
leverage_evidence: About describes tools reading current makeup settings and aggregate color estimates without exposing frames or landmarks.
Agent can create/refine looks, apply coordinated changes and see manual adjustments.
Frames visibly show iterative swatch selection and makeup changes on a face preview.
execution_rationale: The frames clearly show a functioning visual try-on workflow with categories, swatches and changing rendered appearance; end-to-end product search/purchase and agent calls are claimed rather than directly visible.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows multiple makeup states and immediate face-preview changes.
Visible controls include categories, color swatches and action buttons.
About specifies local face tracking/rendering and shared studio state.
impact_rationale: Beauty shoppers and makeup enthusiasts have a concrete desire to preview looks privately and precisely before purchase; local processing also addresses camera privacy concerns.
impact_evidence: Specific use cases include matching products, exact shades and personalized looks.
Privacy design keeps camera and face processing in-browser.
Visible try-on changes demonstrate the core value proposition.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-makeup-artist interaction is a fresh blend of conversational styling, exact manual color control and privacy-preserving local vision.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language requests and precise direct adjustments coexist in one shared studio.
Tool outputs intentionally exclude sensitive visual/biometric data.
Agent can reason from aggregate color estimates while live video stays local.
usability_note: Immediate preview feedback and swatches make the core loop legible; the agent handoff is not directly visible in frames.
red_flags: No submitted video, so agent invocation and purchase-link flow remain unverified.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary paired with genuinely shared conversational/direct manipulation.
advance_reason: Compelling product loop, meaningful WebMCP state sharing and strong privacy-aware interaction design.

one_line: Human-reviewed group food ordering that repairs stockouts while preserving constraints.
what_it_does: Builds a constrained group cart, simulates an unavailable meal, and replaces only that line without breaking budget or dietary requirements.
leverage_rationale: The structured shared cart and narrow repair tool let an agent preserve multiple constraints and modify only the invalidated line; generic UI automation would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About specifies typed build_group_order and repair_unavailable_cart_items tools.
Demo scenario preserves four lines, replaces one and maintains budget/dietary/no-peanut constraints.
Final placement/payment remains a human action.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a deterministic, reproducible complete scenario with exact totals and preserved constraints; screenshots are product packaging only and no video means the claimed flow is not visually observed end-to-end.
execution_evidence: About provides exact before/after totals (€70 to €68.50) and replacement behavior.
Claims shared visible cart and human final review.
Public repo and alive demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Group orders commonly encounter availability changes, and preserving budget, dietary and existing choices is a real coordination problem with clear user value.
impact_evidence: Concrete group-order stockout scenario.
Explicit budget and dietary constraints.
Human retains final decision and payment.
creativity_rationale: The product focuses on repair of a partially invalidated shared decision rather than generic ordering, making constraint preservation the memorable interaction.
creativity_evidence: Only the unavailable line is replaced while valid choices remain.
Conflict remains visible before repair.
Narrowly scoped tools mirror a meaningful real-world recovery operation.
usability_note: The invariant-preserving repair model is easy to explain and review, with human checkout retained.
red_flags: No video; end-to-end behavior rests mainly on detailed written claims.
standouts: Excellent focused scenario showing what structured agent operations change.
advance_reason: Clear, constrained WebMCP-native workflow with strong leverage and credible user value.

one_line: WebMCP security workspace separating agent investigation from authorized remediation.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect repositories, findings and dataflow, propose patches and verify fixes while policy-gating consequential actions behind human approval.
leverage_rationale: The product makes structured capabilities and policy boundaries part of the agent workflow; read-only evidence can proceed while mutations are explicitly held for approval, a meaningful delta over UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About lists repository/security inspection, patch proposal, consequential-action request and verification tools.
apply_fix mutations require explicit human approval through policy engine.
Demo repository includes untrusted prompt-injection content that must not authorize action.
execution_rationale: The security boundary and remediation lifecycle are coherent and specific, but without video the central tool invocation and successful verification are not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About describes a full discover-inspect-scan-analyze-propose-request-verify lifecycle.
Public repo and alive demo are reported.
Frame sheets show a security workspace with repository/finding-oriented panels, though text is small.
impact_rationale: Protecting repositories and production changes from prompt injection and unauthorized mutation is a high-value problem for teams adopting agentic software workflows.
impact_evidence: Explicit untrusted repository content attempts to bypass confirmation.
Read-only investigation versus consequential mutation is a concrete security boundary.
Workflow includes evidence and post-remediation verification.
creativity_rationale: It turns prompt-injection resistance into an explicit product-level authorization model rather than relying only on agent instruction-following.
creativity_evidence: Untrusted content can inform reasoning but cannot authorize actions.
Policy engine gates apply_fix independent of malicious-content classification.
Security remediation is modeled as staged, reviewable collaboration.
usability_note: The staged investigation/approval model is conceptually clear, though dense security evidence may need careful presentation.
red_flags: No video; frame text is insufficient to verify the full remediation flow.
standouts: Correctly separates capability from authority and treats untrusted content as evidence, not permission.
advance_reason: High-impact security problem with a strong, differentiated WebMCP policy boundary.

one_line: Reversible browser extension that reshapes webpages around a user's intent.
what_it_does: Analyzes a page into a bounded semantic model and lets an agent focus, hide, reorganize, highlight or restore real webpage content through validated transformations.
leverage_rationale: A structured semantic PageModel and transformation DSL give agents reliable, reversible control over arbitrary page organization beyond brittle coordinate-level automation.
leverage_evidence: About specifies User Intent to PageModel to DSL validator to deterministic DOM executor pipeline.
Operations include focus, hide, reorganize, task-focused view, highlight and restore.
Every transformation is designed to be reversible.
execution_rationale: The architecture and reversibility are coherent, but no video or submitted frames visibly demonstrate the extension operating on a real external webpage, so end-to-end execution is only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: About gives a detailed dependency-free Chrome extension architecture.
Claims bounded semantic representation and deterministic executor.
No submitted video; contact sheets are not sufficient to verify real-page transformation.
impact_rationale: People regularly face cluttered, inconsistent webpages and could benefit from task-focused views tailored to intent, especially for accessibility and information overload.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies navigation, sidebars, recommendations, ads and hierarchy as page-specific friction.
Restoration and reversible transformations preserve user control.
Semantic transformation targets real webpages rather than a closed app.
creativity_rationale: The concept is an agent-controlled adaptive interface layer for the existing web, with a validated transformation language rather than a chatbot that merely explains clicks.
creativity_evidence: Reshapes real websites around intent instead of building another assistant UI.
Bounded PageModel limits raw-DOM exposure.
Reversible semantic operations form a distinct interaction model.
usability_note: Reversible intent-based operations are promising, but the absent live transformation evidence makes practical usability uncertain.
red_flags: No video and no frame sheet showing the extension transforming a real target page.
standouts: Ambitious adaptive-interface layer with a clear semantic/validated execution architecture.
advance_reason: Original, high-potential concept with meaningful WebMCP leverage, though execution evidence is thin.
